svg.aria-label: Today versus three simplification packages for one pod board. Package B, recommended, goes from 56 to 49 placed parts, 30 to 27 BOM lines per order, pod 7.80 to 6.83 cubic centimetres, arm wires 4 to 2, hand wires 12 to 9, with the 3 volt rail peak falling from 326 to about 92 milliamps. Package A only removes 4 parts. Package C swaps the charger. Package D is a ceiling with 41 parts.
svg.text: Simplification study: today vs three packages, one pod board (rev 1 is the final device)

Each square is one placed part, grouped by function. 2026-10-02. Numbers computed by docs/research/simplify/synthesis.py from hw/pod/bom_jlc.csv (56 parts), sim/checks/size_budget.py and the JLC parts API.

B needs a ~$22 sample set (dock pair, exciters, dummy wire) that O21 forbids buying. Lift O21 for it (recommended) or freeze on the defaults, B3 = B without PER-01D and PER-07: 49 placements,
28 BOM lines, 12 wires / 11 pads, 4 arm wires, still 6.83 cm3.

Costs: JLC Standard PCBA charges $1.53 per BOM line (Basic or Extended) plus setup, stencil and X-ray, so lines and hidden-joint packages are the cost drivers, not Extended types. $/order = parts for 4 boards + line fees + about $10 for not
ordering the pad board (derived, unquoted). Money ranks last (spec O19).

No integrated part replaced several cheap ones: nPM1300, BQ25155/50, MAX98357A and 500 mA LDOs fail on size, D11, package fragility, bridge peaks or D14. Full ranking, ledgers and sources: docs/research/simplification-study.md. ECRs: ECR-0014,
